gap: No result ChatGPT got says that Tripp Lite's Power It! power-strip manual forbids plugging the strip into an extension cord or adapter that drops the ground pin, or into an ungrounded outlet. That rules out the common fix of adding a 2-prong adapter or a second cord to reach further.
standout_why: I compared against rottenwifi.com (result 5, opened). It already says not to plug one strip into another, not to use indoor strips outdoors, and to keep heaters off consumer strips. It says nothing about ungrounded outlets, ground-dropping adapters, NEMA plug types or 20 A circuits. gearlark.com (result 6) failed to open with a TLS certificate error. The Eaton SKU pages (results 7–8), Newegg (9–10, 403), Office Depot (3–4, timeout), Walmart (2, bot wall) and CRST (11–12, 429) would not load, so I could not check what they say. Only part of my finding is new against what I could read.
decides: It confirms the pick rather than changing it. Buy the cord length you need instead of planning to extend a shorter strip, and plug into a grounded 3-prong outlet. On Tessan's own store, its 5–25 ft flat-plug model 1026 is rated 1875 W across 8 outlets, while its 10 ft PS09 and 5 ft PS07 are rated 1250 W. So for a long cord with full 15 A capacity, the 1026 is the Tessan to pick. I could not open the Eaton page for SS361220, so its plug type is still open. If it uses a NEMA 5-20P plug, it will not fit an ordinary household outlet.
